title: Ionis’ ‘breakthrough’ Alexander disease approval establishes pillar of rare disease pipeline
summary: After Jenny Pearson’s daughter Elise first had a seizure at 16 months old, an MRI came back clean—her brain “looked beautiful,” Pearson recalled to Fierce. But a follow-up scan a year later, just days before Thanksgiving, showed her frontal lobe was now awash in white splotches. A genetic test the week before Christmas gave a troubling diagnosis: Alexander disease.

title: Menarini signs $771M deal to take Gan & Lee GLP-1 to European market
summary: Italian company the Menarini Group has agreed to pay Chinese insulin maker Gan & Lee Pharmaceuticals €62 million ($72 million) up front to collaborate on the registration and commercialization of Gan & Lee’s GLP-1 bofanglutide.

title: Chutes & Ladders—Invivyd's chairman adds CEO role ahead of COVID readout
summary: Infectious-disease biotech Invivyd has appointed its current chairman, Marc Elia, as CEO.

title: Psilocybin proves promising in neuropathic pain mouse study
summary: Amid the rise of psychedelics in the mental health space, researchers have begun to explore psilocybin as a treatment for chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy.

title: Pfizer offloads scrapped Seagen ADC to Medicus Pharma in up to $1B+ deal
summary: Pfizer has found a new home for an antibody-drug conjugate it acquired in its $43 billion Seagen buyout and dropped earlier this year.

title: AbbVie’s bispecific T-cell engager shows promise in ph. 3 multiple myeloma trial
summary: AbbVie released positive phase 3 data Thursday showing that its bispecific T-cell engager etentamig improved response rates and progression-free survival in patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma.

title: GSK pens $1.3B Hutchmed deal for early-stage KRAS-EGFR cancer asset
summary: GSK is handing over $110 million upfront to Hutchmed in a deal worth up to $1.295 billion to get its hands on a first-in-class oncology candidate.

title: Ultragenyx fails phase 3 Angelman test, plots ‘significant expense reductions’
summary: Ultragenyx had been flying high after its recent FDA approval for Genglycos—but the company has been brought back down to earth with a damaging phase 3 flop.

title: Fortrea boosts early-phase CRO platform with $45M acquisition of Worldwide division
summary: Fortrea has agreed to acquire the early-phase services division of fellow CRO Worldwide Clinical Trials for $45 million.

title: Novartis telegraphs 130 job cuts amid biologics rethink in Switzerland
summary: Novartis could cut about 130 jobs in Switzerland as it rethinks its biologics technical development and production footprint in Basel.

title: Teva autoimmune antibody notches ph. 2 win in celiac disease
summary: Teva Pharmaceutical's dreams of a first-in-class autoimmune blockbuster are being kept alive after the Israeli outfit’s anti-interleukin-15 antibody scored a midstage win in celiac disease.

title: TScan axes 75% of workforce to make room for solid tumor programs
summary: TCR-T specialist TScan Therapeutics will reduce its workforce by 75% following the pause of its hematological and autoimmune programs.

title: SEC, FDA sign info-sharing agreement as a ‘signal to the market’ on insider trading
summary: The SEC and the FDA have signed a three-year agreement to step up cooperation and information-sharing capabilities, aiming to improve each organization’s regulatory and enforcement missions.

title: Novartis inks $3.2B subcutaneous drug delivery deal with Alteogen
summary: Novartis has struck a deal worth up to $3.2 billion to work with Alteogen on subcutaneous drug delivery, joining Biogen and GSK on the list of drugmakers to pay to access the technology this year.

title: From his parents’ basement to your medicine cabinet: Absci CEO endeavors to create biotech’s Apple
summary: The overwhelming demand for GLP-1 weight loss drugs has reshaped the drug market, empowering consumers to take charge of their own health and removing barriers between their wallets and their medicine cabinets.

title: ESC: Alnylam's next-gen silencer sees silver linings after fallout of AZ, Ionis trial in ATTR-CM
summary: As AstraZeneca appears to close the book on a combo approach following the phase 3 failure of its Ionis-partnered Wainua, several analysts contend it’s too early to count out Alnylam’s silencing drugs in ATTR-CM patients also taking standard-of-care stabilizers.

title: Roche inks $1.53B deal for Simcere’s B-cell-targeting antibody
summary: Roche is paying oncology-focused Simcere Zaiming $75 million upfront for global rights to a preclinical trispecific antibody targeting B-cell-mediated diseases.

title: ArsenalBio sheds most of staff in pivot to in vivo CAR-T
summary: About a year after halving its staff in a clinical push, Arsenal Biosciences is now making a hard pivot that involves laying off most of its employees and seeking out new homes for its assets.

title: Medtronic recalls reflux monitoring device as 184 serious injuries linked to capsule
summary: Medtronic is recalling certain esophageal pH monitoring capsule delivery devices amid risks of them failing whilst deployed.

title: Alumis crushed by midstage lupus flop but plots path to phase 3 for TYK2 inhibitor
summary: A phase 2b lupus trial of Alumis’ envudeucitinib has missed its primary and secondary endpoints. But the biotech is still moving the TYK2 inhibitor into phase 3 in the autoimmune disease, pointing to evidence of efficacy in a prespecified subgroup of patients to support its decision.

title: Neural geometry guides learning
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 04 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02442-6Why some skills are easier to learn than others remains a central question in neuroscience. Busch and colleagues demonstrate that the intrinsic geometry of human brain activity shapes learning, thereby facilitating adaptation that remains within existing neural manifolds while limiting learning beyond them.

title: Neuromodulation for restoring and amplifying brain function
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 04 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02434-6This study argues that neuromodulation should harness the brain’s natural compensatory adaptations, rather than solely restore healthy-like dynamics, providing a framework for improving cognition in psychiatric and aging populations.

title: Priming of CD8+ T cells by peripheral dendritic cells exacerbates tau-mediated neurodegeneration
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 03 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02427-5The authors identify peripheral dendritic cell priming of T cells as a key driver of brain inflammation and neurodegeneration in a mouse model of tauopathy, providing new insights into immune mechanisms contributing to tau-dependent neurodegeneration.

title: Structured experience shapes strategy learning and neural dynamics in the medial entorhinal cortex
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 03 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02409-7The authors use recurrent neural networks to predict how structured prior experience shapes neural dynamics as mice learn flexible timing strategies during complex context-dependent behavior.

title: Glutamate concentration tunes AMPA receptor function through conductance-state occupancy
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02414-wThis study shows that glutamate concentration at synapses can dynamically reshape how synaptic AMPA receptors pass current and calcium. This reveals a rapid way that synapses tune communication in the brain.

title: Mitochondrial calcium influx-driven bioenergetics selectively enable drug addiction
summary: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 02 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02421-xThis study shows that addictive drugs hijack mitochondrial Ca2+-dependent bioenergetics in reward circuits to drive pathological dopamine release, identifying mitochondrial calcium uniporter as a metabolic gatekeeper.
